title: Biomarkers in Patients With Acute Ischaemic Stroke Undergoing Thrombectomy Compared With Controls: A Pilot Study
abstract: Detection of cerebral ischaemia is challenging in patients who are anaesthetised, sedated or have reduced levels of consciousness, as neurological examination is difficult or even impossible to assess. Furthermore, as some patients cannot be transported for radiology, for example during surgery, a reliable blood biomarker for detecting acute cerebral events would be of considerable clinical value. We aimed to compare levels of brain injury biomarkers glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP), neurofilament light chain (NfL), and total tau (tau) in patients with acute ischaemic stroke (AIS) undergoing endovascular thrombectomy under general anaesthesia or sedation to controls undergoing non-cerebral surgery under general anaesthesia. These biomarkers were chosen because previous studies have demonstrated their potential as blood biomarkers of acute cerebral injury and ischaemic stroke. In this prospective, observational pilot study, conducted at the Sahlgrenska University Hospital, Gothenburg, Sweden, between 2021 and 2024, GFAP, NfL, and tau were analysed using the Simoa Neurology 4-plex assay, before thrombectomy or surgery and at 2- and 24 h thereafter. Blood samples from 21 patients with AIS and 19 controls were analysed. GFAP concentrations in patients with AIS increased significantly from baseline to 24 h (median 301.0 → 1443.0 pg/mL; p = 0.001) and were higher than in controls at all time points (p < 0.01). In the controls there was no significant increase in GFAP from baseline to 24 h (p = 0.449). NfL and tau increased significantly in patients with AIS (p = 0.001 and 0.002) but also in the controls (p = 0.001 and 0.047). GFAP and NfL concentrations were higher in patients with acute ischaemic stroke than in surgical controls at all sampling time points, whereas tau differed only after 24 h. Unlike NfL and tau, GFAP did not increase significantly in controls, suggesting that it may be less influenced by anaesthesia and surgery. These findings support further evaluation of GFAP as a potential biomarker of acute cerebral injury in perioperative and critical care settings. A biomarker of ischaemic cerebral injury could be attractive to support treatments to protect brain health during anaesthesia and surgery. In a pilot study, glial fibrillary acidic protein emerged as a potential candidate as it was increased in patients undergoing endovascular thrombectomy for large-vessel ischaemic stroke compared to anaesthetised patients undergoing non-cerebral surgery. ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT03919370.

title: Plasma P-Tau217 as a Prognostic, Monitoring, and Risk-Stratification Biomarker of Clinical Progression in Lewy Body Disease
abstract: Although plasma phosphorylated tau-217 (pTau217) detects co-occurring Alzheimer disease (AD) neuropathologic change in Lewy body disease (LBD), relationships with long-term clinical outcomes remain unclear. Our aim was to evaluate plasma pTau217 as a prognostic, risk-stratification, and monitoring biomarker of cognitive and functional decline in LBD. This prospective longitudinal study included Stanford AD Research Center participants enrolled from 2015 to 2023 with plasma pTau217 data and clinical diagnoses of LBD spectrum, AD spectrum, or healthy control (HC). To evaluate prognostic and monitoring utility, respectively, linear mixed-effect models tested whether baseline level and longitudinal change (2-5 years) in plasma pTau217 were associated with longitudinal changes (2-8 years) in daily functioning (Clinical Dementia Rating-Sum of Boxes [CDR-SB]), global cognition (Montreal Cognitive Assessment [MoCA]), and 5 domain-specific cognitive indices. For risk stratification, baseline plasma pTau217 status was defined using an amyloid PET-derived, LBD-specific cut-point to examine whether participants with abnormal levels demonstrated faster clinical progression in separate linear-mixed effects and survival models. A total of 501 participants (mean[SD] age = 71.1[8.5]; 51.5% female) were included across LBD (n = 131), AD (n = 133), and HC (n = 237) groups. In LBD, higher baseline plasma pTau217 was associated with faster CDR-SB increase (β = 0.30; 95% CI [0.14, 0.45]; p < 0.001), MoCA decline (β = -0.35; 95% CI [-0.57, -0.13]; p = 0.002), and cognitive index decline (all p ≤ 0.028). Participants with abnormal baseline pTau217 had a 0.85 points/year faster CDR-SB increase (95% CI [0.56, 1.15]; p < 0.001), 0.87 points/year faster MoCA decline (95% CI [-1.38, -0.37]; p = 0.001), faster decline on cognitive indices (all p ≤ 0.018), and a three-fold higher risk of diagnostically progressing to mild cognitive impairment or dementia (HR = 3.41; 95% CI [1.60, 7.28]; p = 0.002) compared to participants with normal pTau217. Faster longitudinal pTau217 increase was associated with faster CDR-SB increase (β = 0.24; 95% CI [0.10, 0.38]; p = 0.003). Plasma pTau217 is a promising prognostic, risk-stratification, and monitoring biomarker of clinical progression in LBD, underscoring its utility for clinical practice and trials in mixed pathology groups.

title: Analytical evaluation and method comparison of an orexin-A radioimmunoassay in cerebrospinal fluid: establishing a cut-off value for type 1 narcolepsy and exploring genetic and clinical characteristics
abstract: This study aimed to evaluate an in-house radioimmunoassay (RIA) for cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) orexin-A measurement, establish a diagnostic cut-off for narcolepsy type 1 (NT1), explore associations with HLA genotype, assess the significance of intermediate orexin-A levels, and compare post-H1N1 Pandemrix-vaccinated and sporadic cases of NT1 and NT2. Control samples were utilized to compare the performance of the in-house RIA method developed at Sahlgrenska University Hospital with the commercial Phoenix Pharmaceuticals RIA kit. CSF samples from individuals evaluated for central hypersomnolence disorders were analyzed using both RIA kits. Diagnostic thresholds, intermediate orexin-A levels, and associations with HLA-DQB1*06:02 and Pandemrix vaccination were assessed. Clinical and demographic data were also collected. The in-house RIA yielded significantly higher orexin-A levels in controls (540.5 ± 166.9 pg/mL) than the Phoenix kit (369.2 ± 96.2 pg/mL), with a mean ratio of 1.54. The in-house method established a diagnostic cut-off for NT1 of 153 pg/mL (100% sensitivity, 95.9% specificity), approximately 38% higher than the standard cut-off. Intermediate orexin-A levels (153-400 pg/mL) were found in 9.7% of cases and were associated with HLA-DQB1*06:02 positivity. In the cohort, 75.9% with NT1 had been vaccinated with Pandemrix. Clinical features were similar between vaccinated and sporadic narcolepsy cases. The in-house RIA method is reliable and yields higher orexin-A levels than the commercial kit. Intermediate levels were linked to HLA-DQB1*06:02, suggesting shared pathological mechanisms. The study was not designed to examine an association between Pandemrix vaccination and the onset of NT1 or NT2.

title: Blood-Based Biomarkers as Predictors of All-Cause Dementia: A 13-Year Follow-Up in the Whitehall II Cohort Study
abstract: Blood-based biomarkers are strongly correlated with amyloid positivity in research settings, but their long-term performance in heterogeneous populations remains unclear. Our aim was to determine their long-term prediction accuracy for incident all-cause dementia on their own and when used alongside known risk factors in community-dwelling older adults. This was a retrospective study based on the UK Whitehall II longitudinal, population-based cohort study established in 1985 among civil servants that includes a clinical examination every 4-5 years. Blood samples stored at the 2013-2013 wave were assayed in 2024 for measures of amyloid-beta (Aβ) 42 and 40, glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP), neurofilament light (NfL), and phosphorylated tau protein 217 (p-tau217). Incident all-cause dementia, from 2012 to 2013 to 2025, was ascertained from linked medical records, and Cox regression was used to examine associations of biomarkers with dementia, followed by estimation of prediction statistics. Of the 5,225 (27.2% female) participants (mean age in 2012-2013, 69.4 ± 5.7 years), 516 (30.0% female) had a dementia diagnosis over a 12.2-year median follow-up. Participants with values in the worst quartile of amyloid-beta 42 (Aβ42)/40 ratio (hazard ratio [HR] 1.88; 95% CI 1.57-2.24), p-tau217 (HR 3.74; 95% CI 3.12-4.50), NfL (HR 1.88; 95% CI 1.56-2.28), and GFAP (HR 2.25; 95% CI 1.87-2.72) had higher risk of dementia. The C-index for predicting dementia was highest for p-tau217 (0.693; 95% CI 0.672-0.714), lowest for Aβ42/40 ratio (0.587; 95% CI 0.566-0.608), and was 0.760 (0.738, 0.781) for all biomarkers together. Sensitivity (between 41.7% and 59.5%) and positive predictive value (between 16.4% and 23.5%) of all biomarkers were modest, but specificity (between 76.8% and 78.8%) and negative predictive value (92.3%-94.7%) were good. A second approach to prediction modeling showed a model containing sociodemographic, behavioral, and health-related risk factors to have a C-index of 0.765 (95% CI 0.746-0.785); adding all biomarkers to this model led to a C-index of 0.813 (95% CI 0.795-0.830). The long-term predictive ability of blood-based biomarkers for incident dementia in community-dwelling older adults was modest due to poor sensitivity and similar to that of a model containing known risk factors.

title: Comparing plasma p-tau217 and plasma p-tau217/Aβ42 with CSF biomarkers for assessing Alzheimer's disease pathology
abstract: Plasma biomarkers for Alzheimer's disease (AD) on fully automated platforms offer accessible, cost-effective diagnostic tools. Here we aimed to compare Lumipulse plasma phospho-tau217 (p-tau217) and the p-tau217/beta-amyloid42 ratio (p-tau217/Aβ42) with regulatory-authorized cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) biomarkers (Aβ42/Aβ40 and p-tau181/Aβ42) for identifying AD pathology (Aβ-PET visual read) across a memory clinic (n = 129), a primary care (n = 220) and a research cohort (n = 165). Regulatory-authorized cutoffs were used for the plasma and CSF biomarkers. Plasma biomarkers identified Aβ pathology with areas under the curve between 0.90 and 0.96. Using one cutoff, plasma p-tau217 (83-91%) and p-tau217/Aβ42 (83-92%) had comparable accuracies to CSF (88-90%) across all cohorts (all P ≥ 0.05). With a two-cutoff approach, plasma p-tau217 (90-97%) remained comparable to CSF (91%) in the clinical cohorts (all Padj ≥ 0.12). Results with cohort-derived cutoffs are also provided. In conclusion, regulatory-authorized plasma p-tau217 and p-tau217/Aβ42 demonstrated performance comparable to regulatory-authorized CSF tests for detecting Aβ pathology in symptomatic individuals.

title: Spontaneous Intermolecular Cross-Linking Produces Aβ Dimers With Multiple Alzheimer's Disease Relevant Activities
abstract: Despite success of therapies targeting the amyloid β-protein (Aβ), the molecular identity of the forms of Aβ which contribute to Alzheimer's disease (AD) remains poorly understood. SDS-stable Aβ dimers are present in higher-order aggregates and exert disease-relevant toxicity, but whether dimers form before or after large aggregates, or how dimers contribute to AD pathogenesis were previously unknown. Here, we report that covalently cross-linked Aβ1-42 dimers can form spontaneously upon prolonged incubation of Aβ fibrils and contain isopeptide bonds (Asp1-Glu22 and Asp1-Asp1), the same as those identified in dimers found in AD brain. Importantly, dimer-enriched Aβ aggregates (DEBA) are structurally distinct to dimer-poor aggregates (DPBA) and have enhanced resistance to proteolysis. Functionally, DEBA exhibit stronger binding to microglia, induce transcription of key pro-inflammatory cytokines, nucleate into plaque-like structures with microglia in vitro, and exacerbate amyloid deposition in AppNL-F/NL-F mice. DEBA do not appear to be overtly neurotoxic, whereas solubilized DEBA induce toxicities reminiscent of that caused by Aβ-containing AD brain extract. These findings demonstrate prolonged incubation of fibrillar Aβ aggregates results in spontaneous formation of cross-linked dimers, and this is associated with changes in aggregate morphology and emergence of multiple disease-relevant activities.

title: Circulating angiogenic and cerebral biomarkers for cerebral edema and infarcts in women with eclampsia or severe preeclampsia
abstract: To evaluate whether circulating concentrations of angiogenic and cerebral biomarkers are associated with cerebral edema and infarcts in women with eclampsia or preeclampsia with severe features. This prospective observational study included 45 women with eclampsia and 20 women with preeclampsia between April 2018 to November 2019. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) was performed to assess cerebral edema and infarcts. Plasma samples were collected at inclusion and analyzed for concentrations of neurofilament light (NfL), tau, glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP), placental growth factor (PlGF), soluble fms-like tyrosine kinase 1 (sFlt-1), and soluble endoglin (sEng). Concentrations were compared between women with or without cerebral edema and infarcts. Main outcome measures MRI findings of cerebral edema and infarcts. Among women with eclampsia, concentrations of angiogenic and cerebral biomarkers did not differ according to the presence of cerebral edema or infarcts on MRI. In women with preeclampsia and cerebral edema (n = 4), concentrations of sFlt-1, the sFlt-1/PlGF ratio, and sEng were higher than in women without edema (n = 16), with adjusted fold changes (95% CI) of 4.21 (2.42-7.33), 6.10 (1.42-26.20), and 1.68 (1.10-2.56), respectively. The single woman with preeclampsia and cerebral infarcts had markedly elevated concentrations of several cerebral and angiogenic biomarkers. Concentrations of angiogenic and cerebral biomarkers were not associated with the presence of cerebral edema or infarcts in women with eclampsia. Among women with preeclampsia, higher concentrations of several angiogenic and cerebral biomarkers were observed in women with cerebral edema or infarcts, although these findings require validation in larger cohorts.

title: Comparison of cerebrospinal fluid-to-serum albumin and total protein ratios across automated analytical platforms: implications for subarachnoid haemorrhage diagnosis
A Plasma eMTBR-Tau Immunoassay for Detection of Advanced Insoluble Tau Pathology
abstract: Blood biomarkers that reflect neurofibrillary tau burden, a defining hallmark of Alzheimer disease (AD), remain limited. Endogenously cleaved microtubule-binding region tau 243 (eMTBR-tau243) has shown promise when measured by mass spectrometry; a scalable immunoassay could broaden research access and support clinical evaluation. To determine whether plasma levels of eMTBR-tau measured by a novel immunoassay are associated with tau neurofibrillary tangle pathology defined by neuropathology and tau positron emission tomography (PET). This cross-sectional study included brain donors with antemortem plasma from 2 US autopsy cohorts, and individuals with plasma samples and tau PET from 2 imaging cohorts in Canada and Sweden, with visits between 2002 and 2025 depending on the cohort. Plasma eMTBR-tau measured with an immunoassay and eMTBR-tau243 measured with mass spectrometry. Plasma eMTBR-tau levels across neuropathologic Braak neurofibrillary tangle stages (I-VI, ranging from tangles confined to the entorhinal region to widespread neocortical tangles) and tau-PET Braak stages (0-VI), expressed as fold changes. Correlations with regional tau-PET standardized uptake value ratios (SUVRs; higher values indicating more tau tangles), discrimination of regional tau-PET positivity (area under the curve [AUC]), and correlation with mass spectrometry-based eMTBR-tau243. The study included 728 participants in 4 cohorts (median age by cohort, 71.0-83.5 years; 41.3%-56.6% female). In the 2 autopsy cohorts (n = 241 and n = 240), eMTBR-tau age- and sex-adjusted geometric means were 0.0021 pg/mL and 0.0040 pg/mL, respectively, at Braak stages I-II vs 0.107 pg/mL and 0.101 pg/mL at Braak stage VI (50.5-fold [95% CI, 26.3-97.0] and 25.2-fold [95% CI, 15.8-40.3] higher for stage VI vs stages I-II; P < .001 for both cohorts). In one imaging cohort (n = 99), compared with tau-PET Braak stage 0, eMTBR-tau levels were 11.0-fold (95% CI, 6.9-17.5) higher at stages III-IV and 59.9-fold (95% CI, 39.5-90.7) higher at stages V-VI. Among participants positive for amyloid-β (Aβ) in another imaging cohort (n = 50), the Spearman rank correlations for eMTBR-tau with tau-PET SUVRs were ρ = 0.52 (95% CI, 0.28-0.70) in Braak regions I-II, 0.76 (95% CI, 0.61-0.86) in regions III-IV, and 0.85 (95% CI, 0.75-0.91) in regions V-VI (all P < .001). Immunoassay and mass spectrometry measurements were strongly correlated (Spearman rank correlation, ρ = 0.93 in all participants [n = 108] and ρ = 0.96 in Aβ-positive participants [n = 54]) and discriminated tau-PET positivity similarly (n = 102; AUC range, 0.96-0.99 for the immunoassay and 0.97-0.99 for mass spectrometry). A plasma eMTBR-tau immunoassay identified neocortical tau pathology in autopsy and tau-PET cohorts and correlated strongly with mass spectrometry measurements, a proof of principle that eMTBR-tau can be measured by immunoassay as a marker of advanced neurofibrillary tangle pathology.

title: The GFAP/NfL ratio does not outperform NfL or GFAP in genetic frontotemporal dementia
abstract: We investigated the diagnostic utility of the plasma glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP)/neurofilament light chain (NfL) ratio in genetic frontotemporal dementia (FTD) and compared its performance with GFAP and NfL alone. Baseline plasma samples were available from 391 pathogenic variant carriers and non-carriers, with longitudinal samples (≥2) from 259 participants. Linear mixed-effects models were used to assess baseline differences between clinical groups, longitudinal trajectories, and the ability of the GFAP/NfL ratio to discriminate underlying TAR DNA-binding protein (TDP) versus tau pathology. Baseline GFAP/NfL ratios differed across clinical groups; however, the ratio did not outperform GFAP or NfL alone in any clinically relevant comparison. No significant differences were observed between symptomatic carriers with underlying TDP versus tau pathology. The GFAP/NfL ratio provides no added value over NfL alone as a diagnostic or susceptibility biomarker in genetic FTD.

title: Obesity pharmacotherapies and cognition
abstract: Pharmacotherapies for obesity and type 2 diabetes are increasingly being evaluated for their effects on cognition and brain health. Evidence from preclinical models, observational cohorts, and clinical trials has intensified interest, but findings remain mixed. A central challenge is to determine whether potential cognitive effects arise from direct actions on neural circuits, indirect consequences of improved cardiometabolic health, or both. This Review examines the evidence across cardiometabolic disease, aging, and Alzheimer's disease, focusing on glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1)-based therapies and combination approaches that engage glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide, glucagon, and amylin pathways. We assess how receptor pharmacology, brain exposure, metabolic context, and disease stage shape cognitive outcomes and discuss how mechanistic clarity could guide therapies aimed at preserving or improving cognition.

title: Clinical and Biologic Characterization of a 3-Level Centiloid-Based Classification of Amyloid PET
abstract: Amyloid PET is commonly interpreted using binary visual classification. However, quantitative assessment on the Centiloid scale identifies an intermediate range of amyloid burden not always captured by dichotomous interpretation. The biologic and clinical relevance of this intermediate category remain unclear, despite its implications for biomarker interpretation, prognostic stratification, and eligibility for amyloid-targeting therapies. Our aim was to characterize individuals within this intermediate range using multimodal biomarker profiles and longitudinal cognitive outcomes, as well as deriving Centiloid thresholds for early tau PET positivity, advanced tau PET positivity, and cognitive decline. Methods: We retrospectively analyzed participants who underwent amyloid PET between 2016 and 2024 at the Geneva Memory Center, including cognitively unimpaired individuals and patients with mild cognitive impairment or dementia. Global amyloid burden was quantified in Centiloids, and participants were categorized into low (<12), intermediate (12-37), or high (>37) groups. Group comparisons, receiver-operating-characteristic curve analyses, and linear mixed-effects models were used to assess fluid biomarker differences, define Centiloid thresholds for tau positivity and cognitive decline, and evaluate longitudinal change in Mini-Mental State Examination scores. Results: Among the 512 participants, 202 (39%) had low, 63 (12%) had intermediate, and 247 (48%) had high Centiloid values. The intermediate-Centiloid group showed biomarker profiles, including cerebrospinal fluid and plasma markers of amyloid, tau pathology, and neurodegeneration, between those of the low and high groups. Both the intermediate- and high-Centiloid groups exhibited faster cognitive decline than did individuals in the low-Centiloid group, with a moderate rate in the intermediate-Centiloid group. Thresholds of 13 and 14 Centiloids best identified individuals with cognitive decline and tau accumulation in the mesial temporal lobe, respectively, whereas 51 Centiloids best discriminated advanced neocortical tau involvement. Conclusion: Centiloid-based classification delineates biologically and clinically distinct stages along the amyloid continuum. Individuals with intermediate Centiloid values already show tau involvement and increased risk of cognitive decline, whereas higher amyloid levels are associated with advanced tau pathology. These findings support a 3-level interpretation of amyloid PET beyond binary classification and highlight the clinical relevance of the intermediate zone.

title: Developing the World-Wide FINGERS biorepository for dementia risk reduction trials
abstract: Dementia prevention research increasingly uses multimodal interventions. Harmonized biomarker practices are essential to enable comparable cross-population analysis with initiatives such as the World-Wide FINGERS (WW-FINGERS) network contributing to this effort. To advance globally representative biomarker research in dementia prevention trials, we conducted a cross-sectional, network-wide survey of WW-FINGERS teams assessing biospecimen collection, processing and storage, biomarker measurements, and readiness for harmonized procedures. Most studies (30/39) had or were developing biorepositories; four planned collection and five had none. Practices were broadly aligned, but remaining variability highlights priority targets for harmonization. Clinical biomarkers (lipids, glucose, liver/kidney function) were obtained even in lower-resourced settings. Many studies measured Alzheimer's disease and related dementias (ADRD) biomarkers (blood-based amyloid/tau and neurodegeneration; cerebrospinal fluid where feasible) and increasingly used multi-omics platforms. Evidence-based preanalytical guidance were provided. The WW-FINGERS biorepository provides a world-first platform for harmonized biomarker discovery across diverse populations in dementia prevention, helping to reduce inequities in research participation, accelerating globally representative strategies.

title: Inflammatory biomarker candidates in dementia with Lewy bodies: diagnostic classification, clinical associations, and survival
abstract: Dementia with Lewy bodies (DLB) is a common neurodegenerative dementia that remains difficult to distinguish clinically from Alzheimer's disease (AD) and related disorders because of overlapping clinical features and frequent mixed pathology. Because alpha-synuclein pathology is associated with central and peripheral immune alterations, targeted measurement of inflammation-related biomarker candidates may provide a minimally invasive means of characterizing disease biology and supporting differential diagnosis. We examined whether plasma concentrations of proteins on the Olink Target 96 Inflammation panel differed between participants with DLB (n = 20), mild cognitive impairment and/or AD (MCI+/AD; n = 15), and cognitively normal controls (n = 15), and assessed their associations with clinical measures and survival. Differential-expression analyses, covariate-adjusted logistic regression with receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis, protein-clinical correlations, survival analyses, and pathway enrichment analyses were performed. No protein survived false-discovery-rate correction; nominal associations therefore describe exploratory signals. Relative to controls, DLB showed nominally higher CCL20 and CXCL11. Compared with MCI+/AD, DLB showed nominally lower MCP-2 and IL-2 and higher IL-18R1, TRANCE, GDNF, and IL-12B. AUCs derived from multivariable logistic models containing each protein and prespecified covariates ranged from 0.853 to 0.890 for the DLB versus MCI+/AD comparison. Higher TRANCE was nominally associated with greater motor severity (UPDRS: rho = 0.41, p = 0.0176), whereas its associations with ACE-R and MMSE did not reach nominal significance. Survival analyses identified limited and imprecise associations over a median follow-up of 6.5 years (range 0.07-9.80; IQR 3.49-7.93 years). Pathway analyses highlighted immune and intracellular signaling networks, including NF-kB and MAPK signaling. These exploratory findings support a targeted peripheral inflammatory signature in DLB that differs from normal ageing and MCI+/AD but require validation in larger independent cohorts.

title: Locus coeruleus microstructural integrity and sleep disruption in the context of Alzheimer's disease pathology
abstract: The locus coeruleus (LC) is among the first sites of tau pathology in Alzheimer's disease (AD) and plays a key role in sleep-wake regulation. However, evidence linking LC integrity to objective sleep measures in the context of emerging AD pathology remains limited. Thirty-nine cognitively unimpaired older adults underwent dedicated LC and neurite orientation dispersion and density imaging at 7T magnetic resonance imaging, actigraphy, and quantification of plasma AD-related biomarkers. A subsample of 20 individuals also completed at-home sleep electroencephalogram (EEG) recordings. Lower LC orientation dispersion index, indicating lower complexity in the arborization of LC neurites, was associated with actigraphy- and EEG-derived measures of shorter and more fragmented sleep. These associations were exacerbated at elevated plasma phosphorylated tau 217 and glial fibrillary acidic protein concentrations. Our findings provide in vivo evidence of the LC's involvement in sleep disruption, and they highlight LC microstructure as a potential marker for identifying individuals at risk for AD-related sleep disturbances.

title: A single-center open-label, randomized, parallel-group controlled clinical trial on the long-term effect of the treatment with EGb 761 in blood markers of inflammation and neurodegeneration in patients with mild cognitive impairment: ACE-2020-EGb 761
abstract: BackgroundNeuroinflammation plays a central role in Alzheimer's disease (AD) pathology and other dementias. EGb 761, a standardized Ginkgo biloba extract, has shown potential anti-inflammatory and neuroprotective properties.ObjectiveThis study evaluated the effects of EGb 761 on plasma proteins related to inflammation and neurodegeneration, cognitive performance, and core AD biomarkers in individuals with mild cognitive impairment (MCI).MethodsWe conducted a 12-month randomized, controlled, open-label clinical trial with a 12-month extension phase in 100 patients with MCI recruited at a single center. During the first 12 months, participants were randomly assigned to EGb 761 or no treatment. In the extension phase, all participants received EGb 761 for an additional 12 months. Plasma samples were collected at baseline and at 6-month intervals throughout both phases. Inflammatory and neurological proteomic profiles were assessed using the Olink Inflammation and Neurology panels. AD biomarkers including Aβ40, Aβ42, Aβ42/40 ratio, GFAP, NfL, and pTau231 were measured in plasma. Clinical, neurological, and neuropsychological assessments were performed at each visit.ResultsEGb 761 was associated with nominally significant longitudinal decreases in 15 plasma proteins linked to innate immunity and axon guidance, replicated in the delayed-start group.ConclusionsEGb 761 exposure is associated with longitudinal modulation of serum markers associated with systemic inflammation and neurodegeneration in MCI. Larger placebo-controlled biomarker-driven trials are warranted to confirm whether this translates into clinically meaningful neuroprotection.Trial registration:Registro Español de estudios clínicos (REec) 2020-003776-41, ClinicalTrials.gov NCT05594355, https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT05594355.

title: Decreased awareness of cognitive decline is associated with multimodal Alzheimer's disease biomarkers in cognitively unimpaired individuals
abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) diagnostic guidelines emphasize subjective cognitive decline (SCD) preceding mild cognitive impairment (MCI), implicitly assuming awareness of cognitive decline (ACD) is preserved in preclinical AD. This study aimed to characterize a discrete clinical profile consistent with subtle amnestic anosognosia: decreased ACD, evaluating its association with multimodal core AD biomarkers in cognitively unimpaired (CU) individuals. We analyzed data from CU individuals with baseline CSF biomarkers and 3-year longitudinal neuropsychological assessment (ALFA+ cohort). Decreased ACD was defined by concurrent decline in episodic memory and cognitive awareness using robust longitudinal references (Free and Cued Selective Reminding Test, Memory Binding Test, Wechsler Memory Scale, and Subjective Cognitive Decline Questionnaire). Biomarker outcomes included plasma p-tau181, p-tau181/Aβ42, p-tau217; CSF p-tau181, Aβ42/40, p-tau181/Aβ42, p-tau217; Aβ ([¹⁸F]flutemetamol) and tau PET ([¹⁸F]RO948). Associations of ACD with AD biomarkers were evaluated using linear regression models. Sensitivity analysis was restricted to individuals with memory decline. 350 CU individuals were included (mean age 61 years; 60% female; mean education 14 years; 35% CSF Aβ-positive). Memory decline was identified in 61 (17%) individuals, of whom 25 (41%) exhibited concurrent awareness decline; meeting criteria for decreased ACD. This group demonstrated higher levels of AD pathology compared to the remaining sample. Among fluid biomarkers, CSF p-tau217 showed the strongest association. Neuroimaging revealed elevated frontoparietal Aβ PET, alongside temporal, insular, and frontal tau PET deposition. Sensitivity analysis confirmed that, although less pronounced, this pattern persists at the same threshold of memory decline. This study suggests that assessment of ACD may provide a crucial extension of current AD clinical frameworks.

title: Dysregulated TIE-2 expression is associated with blood-brain barrier leakiness and Alzheimer's disease-related neuropathology
abstract: Cerebral hypoperfusion and blood-brain barrier (BBB) leakiness are related to cognitive decline and the onset and spread of Aβ and tau pathology in Alzheimer's disease (AD). Disrupted angiopoietin/TIE (ANGPT/TIE) signalling causes neurovascular instability and BBB leakiness accelerating cognitive decline and disease pathology in mouse models of AD. To explore ANGPT/TIE signalling in human AD, we measured CSF TIE-1 and TIE-2 levels by ELISA in two independent clinical dementia cohorts, and serum and CSF Tie-1/-2 in paired CSF and serum samples from neurologically normal individuals. ANGPT1, ANGPT2, TIE-1 and TIE-2 levels were measured by ELISA in crude homogenate (CH) and microvessel-enriched fractions (MVFs) of post-mortem human parietal cortex in relation to biochemical markers of cerebral perfusion (MAG:PLP1) and BBB leakiness (parenchymal fibrinogen) in a control, AD, and vascular dementia (VaD) cohort. CSF soluble TIE-2 was elevated in AD biomarker+ve individuals and correlated positively with CSF t-tau and p-tau, and markers of BBB leakiness, neuronal injury, and neuroinflammation. Tissue TIE-2 levels were significantly reduced in Braak tangle stage (BS) III-IV, that is, brains with early-intermediate AD pathology, and were lower in MVFs in end-stage AD pathology (BSV-VI) than in controls or VaD. Lower levels of MVF TIE-2 correlated with markers of cerebral hypoperfusion and BBB leakiness. Our study reveals a reciprocal relationship between elevated CSF and reduced tissue TIE-2 expression that is related to markers of tau pathology, BBB leakiness, and cerebral hypoperfusion, providing novel insights into ANGPT/TIE signalling in AD.

title: Leveraging immunoprecipitation mass spectrometry and neuropathology to identify the clinical value of different blood tau species in Alzheimer's disease
abstract: Advances in plasma-based assays have allowed for the study of several tau and p-tau epitopes. P-tau217 has emerged as one of the most robust markers of Alzheimer's disease (AD) pathology. Despite their strong diagnostic performance, plasma tau biomarkers require further validation to clarify their clinical utility. To investigate the associations between a panel of phosphorylated and non-phosphorylated tau species measured in antemortem plasma and clinical features of autopsy-confirmed AD. Cross-sectional data from 123 participants from the BU ADRC who had antemortem blood draws and brain donation following death. Participants completed neuropsychological testing during life as part of their National Alzheimer's Coordinating Center-Uniform Data Set (NACC UDS) evaluation. AD neuropathology was diagnosed using NIA-Reagan criteria. Time interval between testing at last visit and autopsy ranged from 0 to 12 years, mean = 5.54 years. Raw neuropsychological test scores were used for analysis. Sample size ranged from 65 to 91 across the tests. Plasma samples were analyzed using immunoprecipitation mass spectrometry (IP-MS) for phosphorylated tau species (p-tau-181, 199, 202, 205, 217, 231) and non-phosphorylated tau (195-209, 212-221) peptides. Two ratios were analyzed, p-tau217/tau212-221 and p-tau205/tau195-209. 123 participants took part in this study, 55 (44.7%) female, and 6 (4.9%) Black/African American. The mean (SD) age at blood draw was 78.17 (8.55). The strongest association between plasma biomarkers with neuropsychological test outcomes was observed with the ratio p-tau217/tau212-221 (b = - 0.564-0.404, plow-high = 0.00-0.18), followed by p-tau217 (b = - 0.478-0.377, plow-high = 0.00-0.28), both significantly correlating with six of the eight neuropsychological measures (p < 0.05). Followed by the ratio p-tau205/tau195-209 (b = - 0.513-0.356, plow-high = 0.00-0.55), p-tau205 (b = - 0.365-0.226, plow-high = 0.00-0.44), then p-tau231 (b = - 0.319-0.237, plow-high = 0.02-0.62). Fewer significant relationships and weaker effect sizes were observed among the other biomarkers. The effect sizes of the ratio p-tau217/tau212-221, followed closely by p-tau217 on neuropsychological test outcomes, were observed to be the most similar to the effect sizes of autopsy-confirmed AD (b = - 0.564-0.393). Plasma p-tau217 and p-tau ratios were comparable to autopsy-confirmed AD in predicting clinical outcomes of AD. This study highlights the promise and potential utility of plasma biomarkers for symptom monitoring.

title: The Association of Amyloid-β and Tau With Synaptic Dysfunction in Alzheimer's Disease
abstract: To clarify the relative contributions of amyloid and tau to synaptic dysfunction in Alzheimer's disease (AD). We included 109 cognitively unimpaired and impaired individuals from the Geneva Memory Center with available CSF synaptic biomarkers (neurogranin, SNAP-25, GAP-43). Participants were stratified according to amyloid (A) and tau (T) status, and group comparisons and correlations between synaptic and AD biomarkers were assessed. Multiple linear regression models evaluated the independent associations of amyloid and tau with synaptic markers: Model I (n = 109) included CSF Aβ42 and p-tau181, while Model II (n = 69) included amyloid PET centiloid and CSF p-tau181. Mediation analyses were performed to further investigate these relationships. Findings were replicated in the ADNI cohort (n = 787). Synaptic biomarker levels were significantly higher in A+/T+ individuals compared with A-/T- and A+/T- groups (p < 0.001). CSF p-tau181 strongly correlated with synaptic markers. In Model I, GAP43 was positively associated with both CSF Aβ42 (β = 0.31, 95% CI 0.23-0.40) and p-tau181 (β = 0.94, 95% CI 0.84-1.04; p < 0.001). In Model II, lower amyloid PET centiloid (β = -0.31, 95% CI -0.46 to -0.16) and higher p-tau181 (β = 1.02, 95% CI 0.86-1.19) predicted increased GAP43 (p < 0.001), with the same pattern of associations observed for neurogranin and SNAP-25. The association between amyloid burden and synaptic biomarkers was largely indirect, statistically mediated by CSF p-tau181. Results were replicated in ADNI. Tau pathology showed strong associations with synaptic biomarkers, with a potential mediating role in the association between amyloid pathology and synaptic dysfunction. These findings support a central role of tau-related processes in synaptic dysfunction in AD.

title: Plasma and CSF neurofilament light chain measured by Simoa and Lumipulse: an inter-platform comparison across neurological disorders
abstract: Blood neurofilament light chain (NfL) is an accessible biomarker of neuroaxonal injury, but clinical implementation requires robust analytical comparability across platforms. We evaluated plasma NfL measured by Simoa and Lumipulse across neurological disorders, including paired CSF analyses to anchor plasma findings to the central compartment. We included 383 individuals, comprising healthy controls and patients with neurodegenerative diseases, multiple sclerosis, and ischemic stroke. Plasma NfL was measured in all participants using Simoa and Lumipulse; paired CSF measurements were available in 92 individuals. Lumipulse intermediate precision and between-day repeatability were assessed according to CLSI EP15. Cross-platform agreement was evaluated using Spearman correlation, Passing-Bablok regression, and Bland-Altman analysis. Plasma-CSF associations and age-adjusted diagnostic differences were assessed separately for each platform. Plasma NfL measured by Simoa and Lumipulse showed strong concordance in the whole cohort (ρ=0.90), with similarly strong CSF concordance in paired samples (ρ=0.90). Method-comparison analyses demonstrated constant and proportional bias, with systematically higher absolute plasma NfL values measured by Lumipulse. Plasma and CSF NfL were significantly correlated within each platform (ρ=0.72 for Simoa; ρ=0.77 for Lumipulse). Lumipulse blood and CSF assays showed high precision. Across both platforms, plasma NfL increased with age and was higher in neurological disorders than in healthy controls. Simoa and Lumipulse capture a consistent plasma NfL signal across neurological disorders, but absolute concentrations differ, supporting platform-specific, age-aware interpretation in clinical practice.

title: The antagonistic pleiotropy of tau phosphorylation: plasma tau species in newborns and Alzheimer's disease
abstract: Tau phosphorylation is essential for early brain development but is also central to Alzheimer's disease pathogenesis, suggesting an antagonistic pleiotropy model in which the same biology is beneficial early in life and harmful in ageing. Here, we investigate whether healthy term newborns exhibit higher concentrations of multiple phosphorylated tau species in plasma and compare their profiles against older adults and Alzheimer's disease patients. In this multicentre study, we used the Simoa HD-X platform to measure plasma phospho-tau (p-tau) species (p-tau217 and p-tau205), Glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP), Neurofilament light (NfL) and amyloid-β species (Aβ1-40 and Aβ1-42) in healthy term newborns (n = 42), aged controls (n = 41) and patients with Alzheimer's disease (n = 73). Perinatal associations were examined using multivariable regression adjusted for gestational age and birth weight. In an exploratory subset analysis comprising 12 aged controls and 27 term newborns, 220 analytes were measured using the Central Nervous System panel on the NULISA proteomics platform. Group comparisons were performed using either linear regression or Welch t-tests with Benjamini-Hochberg correction for multiple testing. In the Simoa analysis, plasma p-tau217 and p-tau205 showed a stepwise increase from controls to Alzheimer's disease and from Alzheimer's disease to newborns. Mean p-tau217 concentrations were 2.6 pg/mL in controls, 8.6 pg/mL in Alzheimer's disease and 17 pg/mL in newborns; corresponding p-tau205 concentrations were 0.5, 0.7 and 3.3 pg/mL. All pairwise differences for both tau species were significant. Correlations between p-tau markers differed across groups. Newborns showed a strong correlation (r = 0.81, P < 0.001), whereas correlations were weaker in Alzheimer's disease (r = 0.44, P < 0.001). Newborns also had the highest GFAP concentrations, whereas NfL was highest in Alzheimer's disease and lowest in newborns. Mode of delivery affected GFAP and NfL levels, but not p-tau217 or p-tau205, arguing against birth stress as the main driver of neonatal tau phosphorylation. The NULISA analysis independently supported broad neonatal enrichment of tau. Phosphorylated tau species were markedly higher in newborns than controls, and multiple epitopes, including the brain-derived forms of p-tau181, p-tau205, p-tau212, p-tau217 and p-tau231, clustered among proteins with positive newborn-control differences and strong statistical significance. Our findings identify a high early-life phospho-tau state across multiple epitopes that exceeds Alzheimer's disease levels but occurs outside of the amyloid/neurodegenerative biomarker profile. The results support the hypothesis that tau phosphorylation has divergent biological meanings across the lifespan and motivate mechanistic studies of how the developing brain tolerates high phospho-tau without an amyloid/neurodegenerative biomarker profile.

title: Artificial intelligence applications in microbiota-gut-brain axis research: Implications for Alzheimer's disease
abstract: Alterations in the gut microbiota (GM) are increasingly implicated in Alzheimer's disease (AD) pathogenesis through the microbiota-gut-brain axis (MGBA), influencing neuroinflammation, amyloid-β deposition, and tau aggregation. The inherent complexity of microbiota data necessitates artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) to identify novel biomarkers and therapeutic targets. In this narrative review, we examined AI applications in AD-related GM research, including metataxonomic and metagenomic approaches. AI methods facilitate microbial signature identification and enterotype characterization associated with AD progression, enable multi-omics integration clarifying molecular pathways linking GM dysbiosis to neurodegeneration, support predictive modeling for early AD detection, and inform personalized MGBA-targeted interventions. Employed techniques include classical ML (e.g., random forests) for taxonomic classification, deep learning (e.g., neural networks) for complex pattern recognition, and explainable AI for identifying key bacterial taxa and metabolic functions. Significant challenges persist regarding methodological standardization, larger longitudinal cohorts, and ethical considerations in clinical applications. Future priorities include developing interpretable models, integrating longitudinal multi-omics data to establish causality, and validating AI-derived insights for precision AD prevention and treatment. AI uniquely enables high-dimensional, non-linear analyses that advance understanding of microbiome-brain interactions, though clinical translation requires rigorous validation and interdisciplinary collaboration.

title: Improving the Diagnostic Accuracy of Plasma Alzheimer's Disease Biomarkers With Objective and Subjective Cognitive Screening
abstract: Blood-based biomarkers are increasingly used to identify Alzheimer's disease (AD) pathology and may play an important role in early disease screening and participant selection for clinical trials. However, their performance across stages of cognitive impairment remains unclear. This study examined whether plasma biomarkers differ in their ability to predict amyloid pathology by performance on cognitive screening measures. Participants were older adults from the community-based Vanderbilt Memory and Aging Project (N = 154; mean age = 72 ± 6 years; 37% MCI). Plasma phosphorylated tau (p-tau)231 and glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP) were measured using Quanterix Simoa technology. Amyloid positivity was defined by cerebrospinal fluid β-amyloid 42/40 ratio < 0.072. Objective cognitive impairment was defined as ≤ 26 on the Montreal Cognitive Assessment; cognitive complaints were assessed by a single-item self-report. Logistic regression and stratified ROC analyses evaluated associations between biomarkers and amyloid status, with area under the ROC curve (AUC) values compared using DeLong's test. Forty-seven percent of participants were amyloid positive. Higher plasma p-tau231 was associated with increased odds of amyloid positivity (OR = 1.18, p < 0.001; AUC = 0.73). Discriminative accuracy was significantly higher among individuals without subjective cognitive concerns (AUC = 0.85) than among those individuals with concerns (AUC = 0.67; p = 0.02). Plasma GFAP was also associated with amyloid positivity (OR = 1.01, p < 0.001; AUC = 0.75) and showed greater accuracy among participants with objective cognitive impairment (AUC = 0.82) compared to unimpaired individuals (AUC = 0.63; p = 0.03). Plasma p-tau231 and GFAP were associated with amyloid pathology, but their diagnostic accuracy varied by cognitive screening results, highlighting the value of integrating brief cognitive assessments when interpreting blood-based biomarkers.

title: Alzheimer's disease genetics converges on microglial and neuronal dysregulation
abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is the most common cause of dementia, with global case numbers projected to reach 153 million in 20501. AD is highly heritable, with twin-based heritability estimates of 60-80%2. Although 1,200 causal loci are predicted to exist for AD3, approximately 80 loci have been associated with AD in two recent studies4,5. Low single-nucleotide polymorphism (SNP)-based heritability estimates have prompted the suggestion that little further common-variant risk remains to be found6. Here we analysed data from 109,479 cases, 74,141 proxy cases, 2,131,799 controls and 499,708 proxy controls from diverse ancestries, identifying 118 loci in a multi-ancestry analysis and 9 additional loci in ancestry-specific analyses, 48 of which are new. We identified new AD risk genes, prioritized potential drug targets, and found that genes upregulated in microglia and downregulated in neurons in cases compared with controls were enriched for AD-associated genetic risk. Moreover, we improved polygenic prediction and estimated a SNP heritability of 16%, nearly threefold higher than previous estimates. Together, our findings show that the common-variant contribution to AD has been substantially underestimated, and reveal new molecular and cellular mechanisms as well as specific targets for future drug development research.

title: Short-interval variability and test-retest reliability of Alzheimer's disease plasma biomarkers in a clinically heterogenous cohort
abstract: Assessment of short-term within-subject variability and test-retest reliability of Alzheimer's disease (AD)-related plasma biomarkers is important for real-world clinical implementation and interpretation in research studies. In this study we aimed to assess short-term variability and reliability of core AD plasma biomarkers, proposed ratios, and evaluate a broader proteomic panel. Two serial plasma samples were collected from each of the 92 participants enrolled in observational research studies over intervals ranging from 30 minutes to three months. Test-retest reliability and within-subject variability were assessed for 131 biomarkers measured on three immunoassays (Lumipulse G plasma p-tau217; Fujirebio, NULISAseq CNS Disease Panel and NULISAqpcr AD 5-Plex; Alamar Biosciences). We subsequently evaluated the stability of a dual cut-point approach for AD probability diagnostic categorisation and examined whether within-subject variability was associated with inter-sample interval (time between serial blood sampling). All core AD plasma biomarkers assessed in this study (Aβ42, BD-p-tau181, BD-p-tau217, BD-p-tau231, p-tau181, p-tau217, p-tau231, GFAP and NfL) demonstrated strong correlations (r ≥ 0.79) and high reliability (ICC ≥ 0.84). Within-subject variability was moderate to low for core AD plasma biomarkers. Using a validated dual cut-point approach for plasma p-tau217, most individuals (92%) remained within the same diagnostic category (high/indeterminate/low) across both timepoints, and no individual moved across two boundaries (i.e. from high to low AD probability categorisation or vice versa). For the majority of analytes, within-subject variability was not associated with inter-sample interval after adjustment for age and sex, however, the core AD plasma biomarker, NfL did have a significant association. While core AD plasma biomarkers had limited variability and high reliability over short-intervals, other central nervous system (CNS)-relevant biomarkers showed greater variability, which may be relevant for interpretation in association studies and clinical applications.

title: Transient neurobiological responses to low-level blast during Swedish military special forces breacher training
Plasma eMTBR-tau243 and p-tau205 as T2 biomarkers for biological staging and prognosis in Alzheimer's disease
abstract: Plasma biomarkers that reflect distinct stages of Alzheimer's disease (AD) could enable scalable biological staging. We evaluated phosphorylated tau (p-tau) species across multiple analytical platforms and the endogenously cleaved microtubule-binding region containing residue 243 (eMTBR-tau243) using a dedicated LC-MS/MS platform in a well-characterized cohort with amyloid PET and a subset with tau PET. While T1 biomarkers increased during preclinical stages, eMTBR-tau243 and p-tau205 increased later, consistent with fibrillar tau aggregation. eMTBR-tau243 showed the strongest and stage-dependent associations with regional tau PET and cognition, outperforming T1 biomarkers in predicting cross-sectional and longitudinal cognition. A plasma-based tau staging system integrating p-tau217 and eMTBR-tau243 closely aligned with PET-based tau staging and predicted longitudinal cognitive trajectories. These findings support plasma eMTBR-tau243 as a prototypical T2 biomarker and highlight the potential of plasma-based tau staging for prognosis and therapeutic decision-making in AD.

title: Brain-derived tau in plasma and cerebrospinal fluid after surgery: a prospective cohort substudy
abstract: Postoperative increases in plasma total tau (t-tau) protein have raised concerns that surgery can cause CNS injury. Brain-derived tau (BD-tau) is a novel biomarker that quantifies CNS-derived tau. We assessed BD-tau concentrations in plasma and CSF after surgery to investigate neuronal injury and mechanisms driving increases in plasma t-tau. This was a substudy of a previous prospective cohort study enrolling adult patients undergoing hip and knee arthroplasty. We measured plasma and CSF BD-tau and t-tau before neuraxial anaesthesia (baseline) and at 4, 8, 24, 32, and 48 h after surgery and assessed cognitive performance at baseline and 3 months. Biomarker concentrations are reported as median (IQR) percentage change from baseline. Plasma BD-tau peaked at 4 h with a 254% increase (137-382%, P<0.001) and remained elevated by 31% (6-75%, P<0.001) at 48 h. CSF BD-tau was unchanged at 4 h but increased by 51% (21-82%, P=0.004) at 48 h. Plasma BD-tau was associated with plasma t-tau (β=1.09, 95% CI 0.95-1.23, P<0.001), whereas plasma BD-tau and CSF BD-tau were inversely associated (β=-0.71, -0.97 to -0.45, P<0.001). Higher postoperative plasma BD-tau was associated with both higher CSF albumin and worse cognitive performance at 3 months. Early postoperative increases in plasma t-tau are consistent with a CNS origin but not concomitant neuronal injury. Instead, the early plasma BD-tau increase and the inverse association between CSF and plasma BD-tau could indicate a redistribution of tau from the CNS to plasma.

title: Lower cardiac output is associated with longitudinal decreases in cerebrospinal fluid amyloid-β42, a core Alzheimer's disease biomarker, in women but not men
abstract: Subclinical reductions in cardiac output relate to cognitive decline. We examined the relationship between cardiac output and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) biomarkers of Alzheimer's disease pathologies in 153 participants from the Vanderbilt Memory and Aging Project. Linear regression and linear mixed effects regression models related baseline cardiac output, assessed using echocardiogram, to CSF amyloid-β42 (Aβ42), Aβ42/Aβ40, and phosphorylated tau-181 cross-sectionally and longitudinally. Cardiac output interacted with sex on Aβ42 levels longitudinally. Lower cardiac output was associated with lower Aβ42 over time in women but not men. This may reflect cerebral Aβ accumulation or a more general change in Aβ production.

title: Polygenic scores for longevity in relation to brain MRI measures in a cohort of 70-year-olds
abstract: Population-based studies on the relation between polygenic longevity scores (PGLSs) and specific brain regions on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) are few. We aimed to investigate this relationship in a population of 70-year-olds from Gothenburg, Sweden (N = 675). We constructed two PGLSs (one with and one without the APOE locus) using longevity GWAS summary statistics. MRI outcomes included total grey matter, white matter (WM), WM hyperintensities (WMHs), subcortical volumes, small vessel disease (SVD) score, cortical thicknesses, and fractional anisotropy (FA) fibre tracts. We adjusted for sex, age, principal components, and sex interactions, and corrected for multiple comparisons. We found no associations in the total sample. In males, both PGLSs were associated with smaller WMHs volume and lower SVD burden, and a thicker cortex of pars triangularis, pars opercularis, and insula. Our findings suggest a possible link between genetic propensity for longevity and lower cerebrovascular burden and certain cortical grey matter areas in males.

title: Matrix metalloproteinase-9 is associated with CX3CL1 on tau and amyloid biomarker pathways in APOE4 carriers
abstract: APOE ε4 carriers exhibit heightened pro-inflammatory responses and microglial dysregulation compared to non-carriers. CX3CL1 is a biomarker involved in microglial signaling and Alzheimer's disease. It can be cleaved by proteases such as matrix metalloproteinases (MMPs), which are associated with memory and vasculature remodeling. We examined the role of MMP-9 in the pathway involving the association of CX3CL1 with cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) biomarkers for amyloid and tau in APOE ε4 carriers (APOE4+) compared to non-carriers (APOE4-). We further examined the association between APOE4 groups and inflammatory profiles. CSF samples were collected from 115 cognitively unimpaired VA-eligible Veterans enrolled in the Brain Amyloid and Vascular Effects of Eicosapentaenoic Acid (BRAVE) study (NCT02719327). We found that Aβ42 and Aβ42/Aβ40 were lower in APOE4+ carriers compared to non-carriers. Additionally, p-tau217 was higher among APOE4+ participants compared to APOE4- participants; however, p-tau217/tau was not different between carrier groups. In moderated mediation models, MMP-9 mediated the effect of CX3CL1 on Aβ42/Aβ40, p-tau217/tau and p-tau217/Aβ42 among APOE4+ carriers only. Lastly, we found a correlation between CX3CL1 and a composite pro-inflammatory z score, as well as lower ICAM-1 and VCAM-1 baseline levels in the APOE4+ group. However, CX3CL1 correlated with an anti-inflammatory z score in the APOE4- group, suggesting different inflammatory roles of CX3CL1 in APOE4+ carriers vs non-carriers. These findings suggest that the association of MMP-9 and CX3CL1 plays a unique role in tau and amyloid regulation among APOE4+ carriers, and that early dysregulation of immune systems may occur in cognitively unimpaired APOE4+ individuals.

title: The neuropathy-causing GARS1∆ETAQ mutation drives pathology in subsets of motor and sensory neurons in mice
abstract: Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2D (CMT2D) results from gain-of-function mutations in GARS1, which encodes glycyl-tRNA synthetase (GlyRS), the enzyme responsible for charging transfer RNA (tRNA) with glycine. There are several CMT2D mouse models, but Gars∆ETAQ/+ is the only one that bears a patient-sourced mutation. Created using CRISPR/Cas9 to model a 12-nucleotide de novo GARS1 deletion identified in an unusually severe CMT2D patient, Gars∆ETAQ/+ mice have previously been shown to display several neuromuscular phenotypes: motor axon loss, denervated neuromuscular junctions (NMJs) and reduced muscle function. Here, we extend these analyses to provide a more comprehensive understanding of both motor and sensory nerve deficits across hind- and fore-limbs. At 3 months, Gars∆ETAQ/+ mice possess sex-independent alterations in the levels of neuropathy biomarkers - including decreased NfL and increased periaxin - alongside reduced muscle endurance and strength, and impairments in the sensory modalities of mechanosensation, proprioception and nociception. Underpinning these dysfunctions, we identified site-specific defects comprising altered sensory neuron populations, muscle spindle loss, reduced motor neuron size, disrupted NMJ innervation and maturation, and reduced axonal transport of signalling endosomes in vivo. Together, these experiments show that Gars∆ETAQ/+ mice display robust and selective peripheral nerve pathology that manifests in a general length-dependent fashion, priming this CMT2D allele for testing treatments and evaluating mechanisms underlying peripheral nerve vulnerability.

title: Presymptomatic plasma biomarkers in autosomal dominant Alzheimer's disease: sequence and timing
abstract: Autosomal dominant Alzheimer’s disease (ADAD) serves as a model for presymptomatic biomarker discovery. Characterising the temporal profile of plasma biomarker levels in presymptomatic individuals may enhance understanding of disease pathogenesis, inform future clinical trials and guide clinical interpretation. We evaluated 124 proteins using a NUcleic acid-Linked Immuno-Sandwich Assay panel in 270 plasma samples from a longitudinal cohort study of ADAD, comprising 113 individuals (73 mutation carriers and 40 non-carriers). We determined the plasma proteomic changes that distinguished mutation carriers from non-carriers. We then used predicted age at symptom onset to determine the approximate timing of presymptomatic divergence in biomarker levels in carriers relative to non-carriers. Nine proteins (amyloid-beta 42 (Aβ42), beta-secretase 1 (BACE1), glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP), pTau181, pTau231, pTau217, t0tal tau (MAPT), neurofilament light (NfL) and acetylcholinesterase (AChE)) robustly differed between carriers and non-carriers cross-sectionally. Longitudinal analyses showed elevated Aβ42 levels were statistically discernible in carriers approximately 26 years before expected symptom onset. Carriers diverged from non-carriers in phosphorylated tau markers at approximately 21–24 years before expected symptom onset, total tau at 19 years, GFAP and BACE1 at 14 years and NfL at 6 years. Differences in AChE were seen in symptomatic individuals likely reflecting cholinesterase inhibitor use. Multiple plasma proteins are elevated in presymptomatic and symptomatic ADAD mutation carriers relative to non-carriers. Changes in eight biomarkers occur sequentially from 26 to 6 years prior to symptom onset. Combining biomarkers may help in staging presymptomatic AD and optimise clinical trial inclusion. Further work is needed to assess how these findings generalise to non-monogenic AD.

title: The second assessment of the commutability of candidate reference materials for the harmonization of blood neurofilament light chain measurements
abstract: Blood neurofilament light (NfL) is a sensitive biomarker of neuroaxonal injury, but substantial differences in absolute concentrations across analytical platforms underscore the need for assay standardization. This study aimed to evaluate the commutability of candidate reference materials (RMs) generated by spiking serum pools with cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) to support global assay harmonization. The study included 45 individual clinical serum samples and 30 candidate RMs. The RMs comprised three serum pools, each combined with each of three CSF pools at three concentration levels, in addition to the three unspiked serum pools. Commercial NfL measurement procedures (MPs) from six manufacturers (Roche, Fujirebio, Meso Scale Discovery, Bio-Techne, UmanDiagnostics, and Quanterix) were evaluated. Commutability was assessed using a difference in bias approach. Spearman correlations between MPs were excellent (ρ=0.96-0.99), although regression slopes differed substantially, with differences up to a 46-fold. Across the 450 RM assessments, 62 % were classified as commutable, 37 % as indeterminate, and 0.66 % as non-commutable. Approximately two-thirds of the uncertainty in the difference in bias was attributable to MP imprecision rather than sample specific effects, suggesting that standardization of NfL measurements is feasible. Spiking serum pools with CSF appears to be an effective strategy for consistently producing commutable RMs for NfL measurement. Although the relatively high proportion of indeterminate results indicates a need for improved MP precision or additional replicate measurements, the study supports continued development of SI-traceable reference materials to facilitate standardization of NfL measurements in clinical practice.

title: Correlation of blood biomarkers with microstructural brain injury in survivors of out-of-hospital cardiac arrest
abstract: In-hospital mortality among resuscitated out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) patients remains high. Identifying patients who will benefit from intensive care while avoiding prolonged, potentially unnecessary treatments is essential. Blood-based biomarkers provide a novel method for evaluating brain injury. The ability of glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP), neurofilament light chain (NfL), neuron-specific enolase (NSE) and total-tau (t-tau) to measure white and grey matter injury is unestablished in comatose OHCA survivors treated with targeted temperature management (TTM) or xenon combined with TTM. We examined correlations between the biomarkers and white and grey matter injury assessed with diffusion tensor imaging (DTI). This was a randomized, single-blind, phase 2 clinical drug trial involving two multipurpose intensive care units in Finland. It was conducted between August 2009 and March 2015. One hundred and ten comatose OHCA patients aged 24 to 76 years were randomly assigned to either inhaled xenon treatment combined with 24-h TTM (33°C) (n = 55, xenon group) or TTM alone (n = 55, control group). MRI data were available from 96 patients, with a median imaging time of 53 h (interquartile range, 47-64 h) after OHCA. Biomarker data were obtained from 105 patients. In the control group of 48 patients, after adjusting for age, sex and site, a disruption of white matter microintegrity as measured by decreased fractional anisotropy (FA) of DTI, the primary endpoint of the trial, showed a significant negative correlation with NfL at 24, 48 and 72 h (ρ = -0.28 to -0.37; P < 0.05), NSE at 48 and 72 h (ρ = -0.30 to -0.35; P < 0.05) and t-tau only at 72 h (ρ = -0.30; P < 0.05). In the xenon group (n = 48), these correlations were absent at all timepoints. The NfL-FA partial correlations showed progressive divergence between the xenon and control groups, with a statistically significant between-group difference observed at 72 h (ρ = -0.37 versus ρ = 0.14; P = 0.016). Cortical or basal ganglia grey matter mean diffusivity did not have a consistent correlation with biomarker levels at different time points. No statistically significant differences were found between the xenon and control groups in the adjusted geometric mean levels of GFAP, NfL, NSE or t-tau at various time points following OHCA. In conclusion, NfL correlated with FA in controls but not in the xenon group. This between-group difference reached significance at 72 h, suggesting that xenon may modify the relationship between axonal injury and white matter microstructure after OHCA.

title: Mild Traumatic Brain Injury: A Narrative Review of Blood-Based Biomarkers and Detection Methods
abstract: Given the prevalence of mild traumatic brain injury (mTBI) and sports-related concussion, the development of efficient diagnosis methods is essential. Although magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and computed tomography are standard imaging modalities in traumatic brain injury assessment, they frequently fail to detect the subtle structural and metabolic changes associated with mTBI. Furthermore, while cognitive tests like the Immediate Post-Concussion Assessment and Cognitive Testing and the Sports Concussion Assessment Tool 5 have been developed, fluid-based biomarkers provide a cheaper and quicker method to identify mTBI. Using the PubMed database, we searched for English-language articles on mTBI biomarkers. Conventional biomarkers (e.g., glial fibrillary acidic protein, neuron-specific enolase, tau) frequently show statistically significant group-level differences after mTBI, but their individual-level diagnostic performance is often moderate, with overlapping distributions. As a result, single markers alone may not reliably distinguish mTBI from controls or from other neurological conditions. Biomarkers can detect differences between mTBI and control patients, but the literature suggests that detectors such as neurogranin are not significant indicators of mTBI. Moreover, studies showed that alpha-synuclein increases during the acute phase of mTBI, yet it has been found that lower α-synuclein levels are associated with mTBI in trauma patients. Due to these discrepancies, multi-biomarker panels may be the most comprehensive way to detect mTBI in the acute phase. While some developments are promising, the limitations associated with the current biomarkers warrant comprehensive studies to assess their effectiveness. In clinical practice, these proteins are measured using automated electrochemiluminescence immunoassays that are inexpensive, allow single-sample testing, and yield results in ∼20 min. Access is the constraint, as these analyzers are hospital-based; therefore, point-of-care (e.g., finger-prick) tests remain a priority. Conventional enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay are research tools and are less suitable for acute-care workflows. Attention should be directed toward the development of technologies to measure mTBI biomarkers pitch-side so that head injuries can be diagnosed immediately after injury.

title: Comparison of brain-derived versus conventional pTau biomarkers in CSF and plasma for detecting Alzheimer's disease
abstract: Brain-derived phosphorylated tau species are postulated to improve the detection of Alzheimer's disease pathology by mitigating non-specific increases. However, their true diagnostic performance, relative to conventional CSF and plasma phosphorylated tau assays, remains uncharacterized. The objective was to compare the diagnostic performance of brain-derived and conventional phosphorylated tau assays across multiple analytes (phosphorylated tau 181, phosphorylated tau 217, phosphorylated tau 231) in CSF and plasma, and to examine biomarker differences across amyloid-β status and cognitive groups. This study included 1098 participants with amyloid-PET imaging and CSF samples from the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative, and a subset of 925 individuals with plasma samples. Diagnostic performance of brain-derived and conventional phosphorylated tau assays was assessed by receiver operating characteristic curves, with calculation of area under the curve, sensitivity, specificity and optimal cutpoints. Associations with amyloid-β burden were evaluated using Spearman correlations, and fold-changes between amyloid-PET-positive and amyloid-PET-negative participants were computed in cognitively unimpaired and cognitively impaired subgroups with 95% confidence intervals from 2000 bootstrap resamples. Brain-derived phosphorylated tau assays showed significantly higher diagnostic performance than conventional phosphorylated tau assays at the same phosphorylation site in both CSF and plasma in the overall sample and in cognitively impaired individuals, except for CSF phosphorylated tau 217. While CSF brain-derived phosphorylated tau correlations with amyloid-PET were similar to conventional CSF assays, pairwise comparisons using DeLong's test revealed significantly higher diagnostic accuracy for brain-derived assays. Receiver operating characteristic performance was generally better in cognitively impaired participants than in cognitively unimpaired participants. Additionally, using a three-range method with cutpoints corresponding to 90% sensitivity and 90% specificity, plasma brain-derived phosphorylated tau 181, phosphorylated tau 217 and brain-derived phosphorylated tau 217 had <20% of participants in the intermediate range overall and in cognitively impaired individuals. In summary, brain-derived phosphorylated tau assays improve detection of amyloid-β positivity relative to conventional assays, especially in plasma, and provide robust differentiation of amyloid-PET-positive and amyloid-PET-negative participants. If these findings are confirmed using fully automated diagnostic platforms that are intended for use in clinical settings, brain-derived phosphorylated tau assays may support future blood-based biomarker triage workflows for identifying Alzheimer's disease.

title: Amyloid, p-tau, neurofilament light, and α-synuclein cerebrospinal fluid biomarkers across Alzheimer's disease, dementia with Lewy bodies, and Parkinson's disease
abstract: Mounting evidence suggests overlapping pathology across Alzheimer's disease (AD), dementia with Lewy bodies (DLB), and Parkinson's disease (PD), yet its extent and clinical implications remain unclear. Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) amyloid beta (Aβ)42/40, phosphorylated tau 181 (p-tau181), neurofilament light chain (NfL), and total α-synuclein were centrally measured using fully-automated Elecsys immunoassays in 347 participants (European Platform for Neurodegenerative Diseases [EPND] cohort) and compared between groups. Associations of amyloid and tau positivity with cognitive and motor function were evaluated. Compared to controls, amyloid and tau levels were abnormal in DLB, but not in PD. Amyloid and tau positivity in DLB were associated with worse global cognitive outcomes, but not with motor performance. NfL levels were elevated across diseases, and total α-synuclein levels were associated with tau positivity. AD pathology is observed in DLB, and related to worse cognition, but it is less observed in PD. CSF NfL captures non-disease-specific processes, whereas CSF total α-synuclein likely reflects CSF tau positivity. Results can help patient management in clinical practice and trials.

title: Plasma eMTBR-tau as a robust biomarker for Alzheimer's disease tangle pathology up to 10 years before death
abstract: Scalable and accessible biomarkers of neurofibrillary tangle pathology are needed for Alzheimer's disease prognosis, diagnosis and monitoring. Here, we show that a blood-based immunoassay for an endogenously-cleaved "eMTBR-tau" fragment of tau protein is strongly associated with autopsy-diagnosed Alzheimer neuropathologic change (ADNC) and predominantly reflects the burden and anatomical progression of tangle pathology but not amyloid plaque load despite being most elevated in amyloid-positive symptomatic individuals. Plasma eMTBR-tau was significantly more accurate than plasma p-tau217 in classifying Braak staging and ADNC statuses at autopsy. Importantly, neuropathologic classification by plasma eMTBR-tau remained high (AUC=0.91-0.95) even when increasing intervals between blood collection and death up to a decade, while maintaining superior sensitivity and specificity over p-tau217. Higher baseline plasma eMTBR-tau was associated with worse cognition cross-sectionally and longitudinally predicted faster worsening. These results were replicated in a living cohort with in vivo tangle and plaque neuroimaging. Plasma eMTBR-tau concordance with tau neuroimaging was up to 94%, suggesting surrogacy. Together, plasma eMTBR-tau captures biological signatures of Braak staging and ADNC over a prolonged pre-mortem window, highlighting potential for early disease detection, biological staging, prognosis and therapeutic development.

title: Air pollution is associated with sex-specific longitudinal changes in astrocytic and neuroinflammatory processes linked to cognitive decline in Alzheimer's disease at-risk individuals
abstract: Air pollution is associated with dementia risk, but its role during preclinical Alzheimer's disease (AD) remains unclear. We examined long-term residential exposure to traffic-related air pollution in 226 cognitively unimpaired middle-aged individuals at increased risk of AD from the ALzheimer's and FAmilies ALFA+ cohort (a nested longitudinal cohort within the ALzheimer's and Families parent cohort). Participants underwent baseline and 3-year follow-up cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) assessment of AD, neurodegeneration, astrocytic, microglial, and inflammatory biomarkers. Exposure to nitrogen dioxide (NO2), particulate matter (PM)10, PM2.5, and PM2.5 absorbance was estimated using land-use regression models. Sex-interaction and stratified analyses were performed. Mediation analyses evaluated cognitive and brain-age outcomes. Sex-dependent associations were observed between air pollution exposure and CSF inflammatory and astrocytic biomarkers. Higher exposure was associated with longitudinal increases in glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP) and interleukin (IL) -6, primarily in women. GFAP partially mediated associations between air pollution exposure and worsening executive and attentional performance. Findings support sex-specific astroglial and neuroinflammatory susceptibility to traffic-related air pollution in preclinical AD. The ALFA+ study has been registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (10-06-2015, identifier: NCT02485730).

title: Fluid biomarkers in the evolving care landscape of Alzheimer's disease and related disorders
abstract: Fluid biomarkers for Alzheimer's disease have advanced rapidly during the past several years driven by breakthroughs including development of ultrasensitive and multiplexing technologies and high specificity antibodies. Blood-based biomarkers, such as neurofilament light for frontotemporal dementia and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, and phosphorylated tau 217 for the diagnosis of Alzheimer's disease, are now being implemented in clinical practice, which is particularly timely because of the increasing clinical availability of amyloid-targeting treatments in Alzheimer's disease. Multiple fluid biomarkers are needed to capture the complexity of disease mechanisms for precise diagnosis and to measure the diverse pathologies that lead to dementia, such as vascular, α-synuclein, and TDP-43 pathologies. Moreover, fluid biomarkers can aid in capturing heterogeneity in treatment course between patients, probably due to copathologies or key intermediates, including microglia and astrocyte dysregulation. Increased focus on biomarker-pathology relationships in experimental models will likely accelerate biomarker development and further the understanding of their precise substrates. Future clinical implementation of biomarkers to capture the full complexity of pathologies will likely be facilitated by the expansion of diagnostic methods, development of point of care technologies, and remote sampling approaches.

title: Plasma Biomarkers for Neocortical Tau Burden
abstract: Phosphorylated tau-217 (p-tau217) is now an established plasma biomarker for assessing amyloid-β pathology in individuals at risk of Alzheimer disease. However, its performance in identifying advanced neocortical neurofibrillary tangle burden remains suboptimal. Precise assessment of tau pathology is increasingly critical for the rational implementation of anti-amyloid therapies and developing anti-tau interventions. Improved biofluid biomarker-based tau staging could enhance patient stratification and optimize participant selection for clinical care and therapeutic trials. To develop and validate a multiprotein plasma panel to improve identification of neocortical tau pathology beyond p-tau217 alone. This multicenter cohort study included 2 independent observational cohorts, Swedish BioFINDER study and Translational Biomarkers in Aging and Dementia (TRIAD). Cross-sectional clinical data and blood samples were collected between 2017 and 2024. Participants included 560 individuals spanning the clinical spectrum from cognitively unimpaired to dementia. These data were analyzed from January 2025 to May 2026. Plasma concentrations of 125 proteins measured using Nucleic Linked Immuno-Sandwich Assay central nervous system panel. Advanced tau pathology defined as tau positron emission tomography (PET) uptake within Braak stage V and VI regions. Predictive performance of biomarker models was evaluated using area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). The study included 560 amyloid-positive participants (BioFINDER: n = 431; mean [SD] age, 73.6 [7.0] years; 212 female [49.2%] and 219 male [50.8%]; TRIAD: n = 129; mean [SD] age, 70.4 [8.3] years; 76 female [58.9%] and 53 male [41.1%]). Using multivariable logistic regression approaches, a 7-protein panel was found in BioFINDER to identify tau PET uptake within Braak stage V and VI regions. When compared with p-tau217 (AUC, 0.86-0.88; 95% CI, 0.82-0.94), this multiprotein panel was associated with improved identification in both discovery and validation cohorts (AUC, 0.92-0.94; 95% CI, 0.89-0.98; DeLong P < .001). This reduced the proportion of individuals classified within the intermediate-risk range (between paired sensitivity and specificity thresholds) in the validation cohort by 14.7% to 21.0%.
